blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Severe Tropical Storm internationally named “Champi” intensified into a typhoon early Saturday morning, Oct. 17. It is forecast to bring rains into the country by Monday, the state weather bureau said. In its 2 a.m. weather advisory, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) said Champi developed into a typhoon outside the Philippine area of responsibility (PAR). As of 3 a.m., it was located 2,675 kilometers (km) east of Eastern Visayas. According to Pagasa, Champi is moving west northwestward at 25 km per hour.
